## Summary

On gfx942, the FP4 indexer calls the gfx950 kernels. Those kernels use a scaled MFMA this GPU does not have, so a long prompt aborts. This calls the gfx942 kernels instead.

The kernels are in https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7017.

- [ ] `17 * 23` returns 391.
- [ ] A prompt longer than the indexer top-k completes.
- [ ] GSM8K completes.

Seen on MI308X, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8. Smoke returned 391. GSM8K scored 0.970, 1274 of 1314.

## Overview

If EngineCore dies, `vllm serve --grpc` never exits. Health goes `NOT_SERVING` and every RPC fails with `INTERNAL`, but the process stays up, so nothing restarts it. This adds the HTTP server's engine watchdog to the gRPC launcher.

- The server exits with code 1 within 5s of EngineCore dying.

items.author: zcnrex
items.summary: launches one program per 256 tokens. Each program builds a request-matching tile, so at decode-verify batch sizes (bs 224, 4 tokens each) four programs each hold a 256 x 256 tile.

## Motivation

`expand_prefill_causally_triton` launches one program per 256 tokens. Each program builds a `[BLOCK, next_pow2(bs)]` request-matching tile, so at decode-verify batch sizes (bs 224, 4 tokens each) four programs each hold a 256 x 256 tile. ## Overview

Request validation parses a Lark `grammar` without a tokenizer, so a grammar that names a special token (`start: "ok" <|im_end|>`) is rejected with the xgrammar backend and falls back to guidance under `auto`, although the xgrammar backend compiles it. This PR resolves special tokens with the request's tokenizer during validation. Stacked on vllm-project/vllm#66691 (xgrammar 0.2.9), which the engine needs to match such a grammar.

## Claims

- With `backend: xgrammar`, a Lark grammar naming a special token is accepted and generates (`ok` then `<|im_end|>`, `finish_reason: stop`)

items.author: Hang-get

items.title: [RFC]: Draft Window KV: Dual-Boundary Recovery and Sparse P/D Page Fill
items.author: SSSunzt
items.summary: Proposes decoupling Main and Draft KV cache pools in speculative decoding to reduce replay overhead and improve TTFT by allowing independent cache lifetimes and sparse page transfers.
items.body:
### Motivation.

Main attention requires the full reusable history, while a sliding-window Draft model reads only the most recent `W` tokens. In the original shared-pool design, Main KV and Draft KV share the same physical block pool, cache-hit boundary, and lifetime. This forces Draft to retain history outside its window. When Draft cache state diverges from Main, it can also trigger unnecessary target-forward replay, block allocation, and Main KV writes.

The shared cache-hit boundary also couples Main reuse to Draft availability. A missing Draft page may move the combined hit boundary backw

The Apple Metal "Install from Source" block swaps the pyproject files with

`uv pip install -e "python[all_mps]"` then installs `sglang 0.0.0` without the
`all_mps` extra. The failure is silent until a missing dependency shows up later.

items.title: [Perf][Attention] Cache Triton K/V cache views per tensor identity
items.author: huangsiyuan0422
items.summary: re-derives K/V cache views ( + optional FP8 ) on every attention call across,, and, even though these views depend only on the tensor's storage/shape/strides, which are fixed once the cache is allocated. This adds ~5-7 us of host overhead per attention layer p…
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #64572.

`TritonAttentionImpl` re-derives K/V cache views (`transpose(1, 2).split` + optional FP8 `view`) on every attention call across `forward`, `do_kv_cache_update`, and `do_rope_and_kv_cache_update`, even though these views depend only on the `kv_cache` tensor's storage/shape/strides, which are fixed once the cache is allocated.

This adds ~5-7 us of host overhead per attention layer per step, which is significant on the eager (non-torch.compile) path.

## Fix

Add `_get_kv_views` which derives and caches the K/V views (and FP8 retype) once per `kv_cache` tensor identity

OffloadingConnector has already reserved sync-load budget for it, but its zero-token allocation callback did not refund the reservation. A later eligible 4-token hit can then be sent to async loading. This change returns the unused reservation.

## Claims

## Motivation

Supernode-wide KV cache sharing (roadmap #43098, @hzh0425 @Shunkangz ) needs one engine to read KV pages that live in another engine's GPU memory over NVLink. The two engines are separate jobs with no common `ProcessGroup`.

items.title: [Perf] linker: Fill the restorable-prefix mask with one vectorized store
items.author: Denji-kk
items.summary: builds a 0/1 mask of the restorable prefix lengths on each rank, then all-reduces it with MIN across the attention DP group. The mask is filled one candidate at a time.
items.body:
## Motivation

`UnifiedCacheLinkerWrapper._sync_restorable_prefix` builds a 0/1 mask of the restorable prefix lengths on each rank, then all-reduces it with MIN across the attention DP group. The mask is filled one candidate at a time (`mask[pages] = 1`). A lookup can report one candidate per page, and each scalar tensor store costs microseconds on the scheduler thread.

`MooncakeDirectLinker.load_layer_wise` submits the range gets of every layer group before it waits on any of them. Layers complete only in the wait loop that follows. items.author: indianspeedster
items.summary: The kernel itself is unchanged. The NVIDIA Triton fallback has the same tiling heuristic and is left unchanged here. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
Part of #66163.

### Purpose

Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, a token's output must not depend on the other tokens that share its step. The
Kimi-K3 ROCm AttnRes op (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/attn_res.py`) picks its launch tiling from the batch size:

```python
# Source tiling helps decode, while one-source tiles scale better for prefill.
if num_tokens >= 256 or num_blocks <= 1:
    block_l, num_warps = 1, 4
else:
    block_l, num_warps = 4, 8
```

`BLOCK_L` sets how many source blocks each online-softmax step combines, and `num_warps` sets the reduction layout.
Both change the FP32 rounding

items.title: [Fix] deepseek: Remap block-FP8 weight_scale for stacked gate_up params
items.author: eaglewangao-us
items.summary: In, the helper is applied on the fused + path and on the unfused path, but not on the stacked-params path ( / → ). The Quark checkpoint targeted by #40776 only has block-FP8 attention linears, so it never reaches that path.
items.body:
## Motivation

#40776 added `_resolve_quark_fp8_block_scale_name`, which maps a checkpoint's `*.weight_scale` to the `*.weight_scale_inv` parameter registered by `Fp8LinearMethod`. items.title: [Fix] disaggregation: Bound the connect phase of the retract rebootstrap POST
items.author: qidaye
items.summary: When a decode server retracts a request, it recomputes the prefix by POSTing to the prefill server. The call passes, and applies a single value to both the connect and the read phase.
items.body:
## Motivation

When a decode server retracts a request, it recomputes the prefix by POSTing `/generate` to the prefill server (`CommonKVManager._run_prefill_recompute`). The call passes `timeout=self.waiting_timeout`, and `requests` applies a single value to both the connect and the read phase.

So if the prefill server is down or unroutable, the request is held for the whole waiting timeout (minutes by default) before it is failed, although the connect could have told us within seconds.

## Modifications

- Pass a `(connect, read)` tuple: a 5 s connect budget (`REBOOTSTRAP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S`)

## Overview

When several local workers' GPUs share a socket, their shares oversubscribe it. This PR bounds the budget by the largest NUMA node the process may run on.

items.author: wzhao18
items.summary: Before each scheduling step, it looks at the first 64 waiting requests and moves the one with the fewest prompt tokens not in the prefix cache to the front. Preempted requests rank ahead of all others and arrival time breaks ties.
items.body:
## Overview

Adds `--scheduling-policy shortest_prefill_first`. Before each scheduling step, it looks at the first 64 waiting requests and moves the one with the fewest prompt tokens not in the prefix cache to the front. Preempted requests rank ahead of all others and arrival time breaks ties. Only that one request moves; the rest of the queue keeps arrival order, and preemption is the same as `fcfs`.

## Overview

On ROCm, `indexer_kv_dtype='mxfp4'` is rejected unless `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, although the paged MXFP4 indexer imports aiter's kernels directly and never reads that switch; this PR requires the aiter package (`IS_AITER_FOUND`) instead. items.author: YYuJLiu
items.summary: Restores exact element-wise division in per-token-group FP8 quantization kernels for non-UE8M0 scales, fixing an accuracy regression introduced by a reciprocal-multiply optimization.
items.body:
## Why
#61343 switched `per_token_group_quant_8bit` (and the fused `norm_and_quant`) from
per-element division by the group scale to a per-group reciprocal + per-element
multiply. For UE8M0 (power-of-two) scales `x * (1/y_s)` is exact, but for plain
FP32 scales the second rounding differs from `div.rn` exactly on e4m3 tie
boundaries and moves quantized codes across the 8-bit boundary. The pre-change
code carried a comment warning about precisely this, deleted by the same commit.

## Overview

On ROCm, `_mxfp8_e4m3_quantize_triton` launches one `[64, 32]` tile per MX block, so at decode token counts most of each tile is masked off and a wide row takes `K // 32` tiny programs. items.author: hsthanb4
items.summary: The per-iteration sequence statistics therefore split into two halves that behave differently under replay: - is a device tensor, so 's is captured and replayed; - is Python state, set only while capturing. Once drains the capture iteration and clears the flag…
items.body:
## Problem

With `--cuda-graph-impl full_iteration`, `FullCudaGraphWrapper` captures the whole forward/backward, including `forward_step` / `get_batch`. The per-iteration sequence statistics therefore split into two halves that behave differently under replay:

- `_seqlen_stats_in_iteration` is a device tensor, so `update_seqlen_stats_from_cu_seqlens`'s `+=` is captured and replayed;
- `_seqlen_stats_active` is Python state, set only while capturing.

Once `consume_seqlen_stats_in_iteration` drains the capture iteration and clears the flag, every later replayed iteration reports `(None, None)`

items.author: Kh4L
items.summary: Normalization expands a request into one rid and one scheduler request per sample, so a single request wedges the server. blocks the HTTP event loop while it generates rids: health checks time out and RSS grows to tens of GB.
items.body:
## Motivation

`n` has no upper bound. Normalization expands a request into one rid and one scheduler request per sample, so a single request wedges the server. `n=56442861` blocks the HTTP event loop while it generates rids: health checks time out and RSS grows to tens of GB. `n=1000000` reaches the scheduler, which keeps aborting the fan-out long after the client has timed out. Reported as item 4 of #31597.

## Modifications

- New `--max-parallel-sample-num`, default 1024. That is well above typical client and RL group sizes, and it keeps per-request fan-out at the size of a normal batch.

## Motivation

Multi-item scoring (`enable_mis`, `/v1/score`, `Engine.score`) runs prefill without CUDA graphs or chunked prefill, so throughput depends on the overlap scheduler keeping the GPU fed. Each block was either a device tensor read on the host or a host-to-device copy from pageable memory, and in both cases it waited for the next batch's forward, which the overlap scheduler had already launched. ## Motivation

items.title: [Feat] diffusion/sana-video2: Support sequence parallelism
items.author: cr-gao
items.summary: Adds sequence parallelism to SANA-Video 2.0, shard-by-token across GPUs so each rank handles only part of the spatial sequence instead of recomputing everything on every GPU.
items.body:
## Motivation

Native SANA-Video 2.0 runs on one GPU only: with `--num-gpus 2` every rank computes the full sequence. A 1280x736, 193-frame, 50-step request takes about 363 s on one A800.

The model is a good fit for sequence parallelism. Its blocks are LayerNorm, self-attention, cross-attention and SwiGLU, with no convolution after the patch embedding. In the 24 linear-attention layers, tokens are coupled only through the sum `sum_j v_j k_j^T`, whose size does not depend on the sequence length, so one all-reduce per layer is enough. The 8 softmax anchor layers need a token/head exchange.

items.author: gau-nernst

items.body:
# [Core] Add `--independent-data-parallel` to run MoE DP ranks as independent replicas

## Purpose

With `--data-parallel-size N`, a MoE model's DP ranks are never independent. Without `--enable-expert-parallel`, the expert layers are tensor-parallel across all `DP × TP` GPUs. With it, they are expert-parallel across the same GPUs. In both cases every MoE layer runs collectives across the DP ranks, and the ranks step in lockstep, with dummy forward passes on idle ranks. Dense models instead run each DP rank as an independent replica behind one endpoint.

This PR adds that mode for MoE models.

items.title: [ROCm][Disagg][CI] Set token budgets for the MiniMax-M3 wide-EP cells
items.author: avininjamay8
items.summary: Reduces --max-num-batched-tokens to 2048/64 for MiniMax-M3 MXFP8 wide-EP CI cells, cutting eval time from ~1h to minutes by shrinking the AITER MXFP8 MoE padded buffer.
items.body:
## Purpose

The MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 wide-EP cells are very slow. The 2P2D EP16 GSM8K eval takes about 1h37 in CI and the 1P1D EP8 one about an hour. The AITER MXFP8 MoE kernel runs over a padded buffer sized by `--max-num-batched-tokens`, 131072 rows at the default, so every prefill and decode step pays for the whole buffer. Small token budgets shrink it. This sets 2048 for prefill and 64 for decode, and the evals drop to a couple of minutes.

## Changes

`models.yaml`: the MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 `ep:` flags gain `--max-num-batched-tokens 2048` (prefill) and `--max-num-batched-tokens 64` (decode)

## Overview

Draft, to discuss the approach. When every request has a top-k, the target distribution is zero outside each row's at most k kept tokens. This PR lets the Triton top-k/top-p kernel write those tokens compactly (ids, logits, count) instead of writing `-inf` over the row. The existing Gumbel sampling and spec-decode rejection sampling kernels (MRV2) then read only those tokens. The path is used by default on CUDA whenever a batch is eligible.

## Overview

With an fp8 KV cache and a backend that takes a bf16 query (`supports_quant_query_input` clear: TRITON_MLA), Kimi-K3's `MultiHeadLatentAttention._decode_concat_cache` dequantizes the fused kernel's fp8 query through fp32 (`(mqa_q.to(torch.float32) * self._q_scale).to(bf16)`, from #51860), which costs three launches and two fp32 temporaries over `[B, H, 576]` per MLA layer per decode step. This PR casts fp8 → bf16 directly and scales in place by the host-side `_q_scale_float`, skipping the multiply when the scale is 1.0, with bit-identical output.

## Claims

- Bit-identical output

items.summary: On gfx950, keeps the small-head Gluon decode only when the per-rank head count divides 16, so Kimi-K3 / Kimi-K3.1-Pro at TP8 (12 heads per rank) and TP16 (6) take the asm persistent decode, which copies the query out to 16 heads every step and slices the outpu…
items.body:

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Stop subtracting image tokens from the per-item video budget
items.author: subhashpolisetti
items.summary: Removes incorrect image-token subtraction from per-item video budget for GLM-4.1V/4.5V, Ovis2.5, InternVL, and Intern-S1, fixing false encoder-cache rejections.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

GLM-4.1V/4.5V, Ovis2.5, InternVL and Intern-S1 subtract a full-size image from the per-item video budget, so a video-only prompt that fits `max_model_len` is rejected with "exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size". items.title: [Fix] scheduler: Prevent pool accounting desync on finished_len trim
items.author: devtyagi3909
items.summary: when extensions terminate a request early and retroactively trim (e.g. repetition detection or loop-abort trimming), could shrink below.
items.body:
closes #49174

### why
when extensions terminate a request early and retroactively trim `finished_len` (e.g. repetition detection or loop-abort trimming), `owned_kv_len` could shrink below `cache_protected_len`. during `release_kv_cache`, `_release_overallocated_kv_indices` then freed pages belonging to the tree-protected prefix, corrupting the token-to-kv pool and triggering invariant checker failures with negative residue (`total_accounted < total`).

### what changed
1. added `Req.finish_with_trim(finished_len, reason)` so extensions have a supported api to finish early with output trimming

vLLM has two merged snapshot entry points:

- `/checkpoint/*` from [#62570](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62570) prepares and restores a running engine while keeping weights resident.

This PR builds on @matteso1's [#59832](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59832) session/recovery draft and extracts the shared engine-side components. The CLI and checkpoint are the only consumers

items.title: [Bugfix] Use max_split_size_mb:21 so freed 1-10 MiB tensors are reused
items.author: viktorkou
items.summary: Raises PyTorch caching allocator max_split_size_mb from 20 to 21 so small freed tensors are reused during model loading, eliminating ~964K OOM retries and cutting load time from 690s to 97s.

## Overview

`Worker.load_model` and `profile_run` scope the caching allocator to `max_split_size_mb:20` (#41268, #58430). - Freed 1–10 MiB tensors are reused under the load/profile split limit again, instead of each stranding a 20 MiB segment.

items.title: [Kernel] Fuse the elementwise chain around get_top_tokens' all-gather
items.author: phambinhfin
items.summary: shards the vocab argmax so the all-gather carries instead of, but it spends the saving on bookkeeping: eight elementwise kernels pack and unpack the gathered pairs. That fixed cost made it slower than a plain full-vocab argmax below ~26 rows.
items.body:
## Overview

`LogitsProcessor.get_top_tokens` shards the vocab argmax so the all-gather carries `[batch, 2]` instead of `[batch, vocab]`, but it spends the saving on bookkeeping: eight elementwise kernels pack and unpack the gathered `(value, index)` pairs. That fixed cost made it slower than a plain full-vocab argmax below ~26 rows. Replace the chain with one Triton kernel on each side of the all-gather.

## Claims

- 1.30-1.36x faster than the current implementation from batch 1 to 128, and never slower (1.02x at 512).
- The crossover is gone: the local reduction now beats a full-vocab argma

MiniMax-M3 on TP8 falls into repetitive loops in normal mode (AIME25 0/30). Answers start fine, then repeat one line until the 32,768-token cap.

## Overview

`--logging-config.formatter json` (#58739, issue #58171) switches Python's log handler to one JSON object per line for log collection. Since #66119 the Rust frontend reads `--logging-config` but accepts only `formatter: text`, so an operator who set `json` for their log pipeline cannot start the server, under both `vllm-rs serve` and the Python-supervised `--args-json`. This PR accepts `json` and writes the Rust frontend's own logs as JSON lines with Python's top-level keys.

items.author: Ranoobaba

items.body:

## Overview

`/tokenize` now treats `tools: []` like omitted tools, as `/v1/chat/completions` has since #65547.
Before this change, a chat template that tests `tools is not none` rendered tool instructions on `/tokenize` but not on the chat route, so `/tokenize` counts did not match the prompt chat actually serves.

**Why it matters:** `/tokenize` disagrees with chat by 100+ tokens for `tools: []` on popular templates; this makes it agree, using the rule #65547 already added for chat.
Clients use `/tokenize` to check context limits, estimate cost and route reques

items.author: amd-pedghazi

items.title: [Fix] [XPU] graph: fake registration for optional MLA kernels
items.author: fumiama
items.summary: When SGLang is built with, the optional operator is not registered. XPU graph initialization still attempted to register its fake implementation unconditionally, causing Torch to raise an error and preventing the graph runner from initializing.
items.body:
## Motivation

When SGLang is built with `USE_MLA=OFF`, the optional `sgl_kernel::flash_mla_decode` operator is not registered. XPU graph initialization still attempted to register its fake implementation unconditionally, causing Torch to raise an error and preventing the graph runner from initializing. Optional MLA kernels should not be required for graph initialization; FMHA registration remains mandatory.

## Modifications

- Register the `flash_mla_decode` fake implementation only when its operator schema exists.
- Keep FMHA fake registration unconditional.
- Add CPU CI regressions using r

items.title: [#21912][perf] Avoid full priority-queue scans for bounded peeks
items.author: Hang-get
items.summary: Priority scheduling with KV-balanced attention-DP admission calls every admitting iteration. The existing implementation scans the entire waiting queue even though the admission window is normally 32 requests.
items.body:
## Description

Priority scheduling with KV-balanced attention-DP admission calls `PriorityWaitingQueue.peek_requests` every admitting iteration. The existing `heapq.nsmallest` implementation scans the entire waiting queue even though the admission window is normally 32 requests.

Use a best-first frontier over the existing min-heap for bounded peeks. It visits only the relevant heap branches, reducing the bounded path from O(n log k) to O(k log k) without mutating or copying the source heap. Requests for at least one quarter of the queue retain the existing `nsmallest` path.

Closes #21912.

items.title: fix(inference): reserve recurrent-state dummy slot when tp_ep > 1
items.author: lauradang
items.summary: A hybrid (Mamba) engine with TP > 1 and EP = 1 (e.g. TP=2, EP=1) can crash with. [Discussion: Auto-sync is disabled for draft pull requests in this repository.]
items.body:
## What

A hybrid (Mamba) engine with TP > 1 and EP = 1 (e.g. TP=2, EP=1) can crash with `No free recurrent-state slots for 1 expert-parallel dummy request(s)`.

The engine's work consensus runs over the `tp_ep` group (expert TP x EP), and between refreshes it reuses a cached result. After local work drains, the stale cache can still say "there is work", so the engine runs a dummy forward. That dummy forward needs a recurrent-state slot, but the dedicated dummy slot was only reserved for EP > 1. On a prefill engine whose slots are all held by pending KV handoffs, allocation fails.

**The fix.*

Megatron pads the output layer to a multiple of `make_vocab_size_divisible_by × TP`. `calculate_log_probs_and_entropy` and `calculate_topk_log_probs` normalize over every column, padding included, but SGLang normalizes over the real `vocab_size`. items.title: Fix dataloader checkpoint directory creation on every writing rank
items.author: jwills
items.summary: When external dataloader state is saved per data-parallel rank, only DP rank 0 currently creates the checkpoint's parent directory. A distributed barrier synchronizes ranks but does not guarantee directory visibility across node-local filesystem mounts.
items.body:
When external dataloader state is saved per data-parallel rank, only DP rank 0 currently creates the checkpoint's parent directory. A distributed barrier synchronizes ranks but does not guarantee directory visibility across node-local filesystem mounts. A nonzero writing rank can therefore reach `torch.save` without its parent directory and fail.

Call `ensure_directory_exists` on every rank that writes a state file. Rank-independent loaders retain their rank-0-only writes. Extend the explicit-process-groups regression test, which uses DP rank 3, to assert that the parent directory exists.

items.body:
## Summary
On DGX Spark (unified memory), cudaMemGetInfo does not report reclaimable page cache as free, so KV cache profiling counts the checkpoint's page cache as "used outside torch" and gives large-checkpoint models a KV cache of a few GiB. On integrated GPUs, read free memory as max(cudaMemGetInfo free, MemAvailable) capped at total for the two KV profiling measurements. Discrete GPUs are unchanged; free_gpu_memory_fraction is applied as before.

Fixes https://nvbugs/7028465

### What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in FSDP engine option, `response_only_lm_head` (default `false`). RL losses read values only at response tokens, but the engine projects every packed token through the LM head. With the option on, the engine passes the packed rows that predict response tokens to the model as Transformers' `logits_to_keep`, so the eager and fused LM heads project only those rows. The values at response tokens are unchanged.

The saving grows with the prompt's share of each sequence: it is largest for long prompts with short responses and small for short prompts with long

items.title: [ray] fix: prevent master port races during worker startup
items.author: SeptPonts
items.summary: Prevent during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore. Previously, probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Prevent `EADDRINUSE` during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore.

Previously, `RayWorkerGroup` probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers. Another process could claim that port before rank zero initialized its process group.

Rank zero now binds and retains the actual TCPStore before invoking the user worker constructor. It publishes the bound endpoint before that constructor can block waiting for peers, allowing the driver to start the remaining ranks.

items.title: Fix math_dapo Minerva extraction for markdown-decorated answers
items.author: siddhant-rajhans
items.summary: The existing regex captures the markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0. Fixes #8449 ## Root cause The Minerva answer pattern matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line.
items.body:
## Bug

Models commonly wrap the Minerva `Answer:` label in markdown bold/italic (`**Answer:** 42`, `Answer: **42**`, `**Answer:**\n\n42`). The existing regex captures the `*` markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0.

Fixes #8449

## Root cause

The Minerva answer pattern `(?i)Answer\s*:\s*([^\n]+)` matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line. When models decorate with markdown:

| Input | Extracted | After normalize | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| `**Answer:** 42` | `** 42` | `**42` | -1.0 |
| `Answer: **42**` | `**42**` | `**42**` |

items.author: zgh-99
items.summary: Starts all distillation teachers at once instead of one after another, which is what dominates startup when the recipe has many teachers. used to build one per teacher in a plain loop, and each constructor blocked until that teacher's vLLM servers were fully u…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Starts all distillation teachers at once instead of one after another, which is what dominates startup when the recipe has many teachers.

items.body:
## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

With valid finite log-probabilities near -0.1, I reproduced a value of -1.4901161e-8 where an 80-digit reference gives 4.9986626e-11. The helper feeds the reported KL term and configured KL loss/reward paths; the Search-R1 example selects `low_var_kl` with a nonzero KL-loss coefficient.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8433.

`SFTTrainer` built its train/val `StatefulDataLoader`s without a `generator`, so every iterator construction drew a `base_seed` from the global CPU RNG. On resume that draw happens right after the checkpoint manager restores `torch.get_rng_state()`, so the resumed run continued from a different global CPU RNG state than an uninterrupted run. This PR gives each dataloader its own seeded `torch.Generator`, so building iterators no longer touches the global CPU RNG and the restored state is the one training actually continues with.

items.body:
## Problem

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

How it happens:

- slime's colocated sender calls `update_weights_from_tensor` with `serialized_named_tensors`, `load_format="flattened_bucket"` and `weight_version`. It sets neither `selector` nor `disable_draft_model`.
- SGLang then fans the update out to every runner, because its default is `selector="all"`. The DFLASH worker

### What does this PR do?

Before a weight sync, `abort_all_requests()` waits for `_admitting == 0` (no request is between the submission gate and the engine) and only then calls `pause_generation()`. `generate()` decremented `_admitting` only on the request's **first output**, i.e. once it had been scheduled and prefilled. items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds `sharded_nixl`, a checkpoint engine for disaggregated rollout with no trainer-side all-gather. Every trainer rank (FSDP or Megatron) exports only the shards it holds and NIXL-WRITEs them into the rollout workers' staging buffers. Each rollout worker reports what it loads (pipeline stage, resident experts and, for vLLM TP>1, its slice of each tensor) and receives only that. The bucket layout is built on the first sync and cached, so later syncs send no per-tensor metadata. Design: `docs/advance/sharded_nixl_weight_sync.md`.

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

`_wait_server_healthy()` calls `requests.get(.../health)` without a timeout. If the server accepts the connection but does not respond, startup polling blocks inside that request and cannot reach `is_process_alive()`.

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

## Background

## Solution

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

items.body:
## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

items.title: fix(megatron): compact actor logits before projection
items.author: liuhao-labs
items.summary: Long masked prompts still produce full vocabulary logits before Slime selects trainable tokens, causing the projection and fp32 conversion peaks in #2253. Add opt-in to project only the loss-masked rows for eligible built-in actor policy/SFT paths.
items.body:
## Summary

Long masked prompts still produce full `[T, V]` vocabulary logits before Slime selects trainable tokens, causing the projection and fp32 conversion peaks in #2253. Add opt-in `--compact-actor-logits` to project only the `N` loss-masked rows for eligible built-in actor policy/SFT paths.

A Slime-owned `CompactLogitsGPTModel` is selected only for eligible actor post-process chunks. Log-probability/entropy computation accepts `[N, V]`, builds compact top-p masks, and scatters scalar results back to the existing response/CP layout. Empty masks retain zero-gradient connections.

items.author: liuhao-labs

## Summary

Max-length filtering already tokenizes every retained text prompt, but default rollout preparation encodes the same rendered prompt again. Reuse those IDs for stock training and evaluation, eliminating the second encoding pass.

The cache contains only immutable packed uint32 IDs (4 bytes per token). Deep-copied siblings share the payload and each materializes its own mutable token list on consumption. The cache is excluded from serialization and dataclass reconstruction. Multimodal outputs and custom rollout/generate/data-source contracts remain uncached.

## 摘要

感谢维护 slime。这个 PR 为 disaggregated `train_async.py` 增加一个默认关闭、fail-closed 的
`--rs-batch-refill` 路径，用于在 sequence-level / geometric rejection sampling（RS）之后，按完整
prompt group 精确补齐 optimizer step 的 effective batch。

items.title: fix(rollout): normalize fan-out rewards by trajectory
items.author: sxl1993
items.summary: This change computes the trajectory-level baseline from [1, 0] as 0.5 and broadcasts [0.5, 0.5, 0.5, -0.5]. The default reward post-processing path is unchanged. [Discussion: @zhuzilin Please review #2302.]
items.body:
## Summary
- count each unique rollout once in the custom fan-out GRPO baseline
- broadcast the normalized trajectory reward to all emitted samples
- reject inconsistent sibling rewards and handle singleton groups without NaNs

## Motivation
For rewards [1, 1, 1, 0], where the first three samples belong to one rollout, the old hook used a sample-weighted baseline of 0.75. This change computes the trajectory-level baseline from [1, 0] as 0.5 and broadcasts [0.5, 0.5, 0.5, -0.5].

The default reward post-processing path is unchanged.

## Test
- added a CPU regression case to tests/test_sample.py
discussion: @zhuzilin Please review #2302. It fixes reward normalization for fan-out GRPO by normalizing per trajectory. The main thing to check is the rollout_id grouping logic.

## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.

## What

Introduce a hardware-platform abstraction so a single `tests/test_*.py` runs on both
GPU and NPU. `execute_train()` dispatches by device — `VIME_TEST_DEVICE` (set by CI),
else `is_npu()`. The **GPU/CUDA path is byte-identical to upstream and needs no config**;
non-CUDA delegates to a vime-owned launcher.

Part of the NPU CI effort — RFC #315 , on top of the pipeline merged in #316.

## Summary

1.Replace VIME's custom colocated IPC weight-sync implementation with the native weight transfer engines provided by vLLM and vLLM-Ascend.
This removes the manual IPC handle gathering, serialization, and worker-side chunk loading path while aligning colocated weight updates with vLLM's native /update_weights lifecycle.

2.Fix fused MoE weight shape mismatches during layerwise reload on Ascend NPU.
